name: AeroVision NDE
tagline: Turns raw NDE scan data into defect maps and disposition calls.
examplePrompt: Analyze this UT thickness dataset from a pressure vessel shell scan and flag any readings below the 6.2mm minimum retirement thickness per API 510.
exampleResult: 2 of 5 grid points below retirement thickness (6.0mm, 5.9mm) — recommend CML re-survey before next run.
how: Python inspection-data parser layered on a structured LLM reasoning pass, cross-checked against API 510/570 thickness tables.
forWhat: Turning raw UT/RT scan exports into pass/fail defect maps and re-inspection intervals for pressure vessels and piping.
where: Validated on offshore platform shell inspections and refinery piping turnaround data.
why: Inspectors spend hours cross-referencing raw thickness grids by hand — this collapses that into a flagged, code-referenced output in one pass.

name: Nexus PM-Copilot
tagline: Builds critical-path schedules from a flat task list — no Gantt software required.
examplePrompt: Build a critical path schedule for this fabrication project — 14 tasks with durations and dependencies — and flag the tasks with zero float.
exampleResult: Critical path: T1 → T2 → T5 → T9 (41 days). 3 tasks carry zero float — procurement lead time is your bottleneck.
how: Deterministic CPM (critical path method) engine wrapped in a prompt interface, so the LLM parses your task list into a scheduling graph.
forWhat: Fast critical-path and float analysis for fabrication and construction schedules, without opening scheduling software.
where: Tested against structural fabrication schedules for tank and frame projects.
when: Built Q1 2025, in active pilot since Q2 2025.
why: Most teams describe schedules in plain task lists before anyone builds the formal Gantt chart — this reads the plain list directly.

name: StructurAI FEA
tagline: Runs static structural checks and returns stress, deflection, and safety factor.
examplePrompt: Run a static structural check on this steel frame under combined dead, live, and wind load per SNI 1729, and return max von Mises stress, deflection, and safety factor.
exampleResult: Max von Mises: 178 MPa. Max deflection: L/312. Safety factor: 1.4 — passes SNI 1729, tightest at the mid-span connection.
how: Structured prompt interface over an FEA mesh-and-solve pipeline, with load combination logic matched to code (SNI/AISC).
forWhat: Static structural verification of steel frames and support structures — stress, deflection, and safety factor in one pass.
where: Validated against clarifier tank frame and structural steel platform designs.
why: Standard LLMs guess at structural numbers. This routes the actual load and mesh math through a solver, so the output is a real calculation, not a plausible-sounding one.

name: Spectra Lab Analyzer
tagline: Reads raw test data and returns spec-classified mechanical properties.
examplePrompt: Interpret this tensile test stress-strain dataset and report yield strength, UTS, and elongation per ASTM E8, then classify against A36 spec.
exampleResult: Yield: 262 MPa. UTS: 415 MPa. Elongation: 24%. Meets ASTM A36 minimums on all three.
how: Curve-fitting and property extraction logic wrapped around raw lab exports (tensile, hardness, spectrometry), checked against ASTM/ISO thresholds.
forWhat: Converting raw test-machine output into pass/fail material classifications without manual spreadsheet work.
where: Tested on tensile and hardness data from structural steel batch testing.
when: Built Q1 2024, in production use since Q3 2024.
why: Lab techs re-derive the same numbers from raw curves on every batch — this automates the read without touching the underlying data.

name: Sentinel QA/QC
tagline: Checks weld and dimensional inspection data against code and drafts NCRs.
examplePrompt: Review this weld inspection log and RT film index against AWS D1.1 acceptance criteria, and draft any non-conformance reports needed.
exampleResult: W-014: porosity 2.1mm exceeds 1.6mm allowable — NCR-014 drafted, reject and re-weld recommended.
how: Rule engine encoding AWS/ASME acceptance criteria, layered under an LLM interface that reads inspection logs and drafts NCR language.
forWhat: Weld and dimensional QA/QC surveillance during fabrication — accept/reject calls with a paper trail.
where: Tested on structural steel fabrication shop-floor inspection logs.
why: QA inspectors already keep the data — this saves the time spent manually cross-referencing every defect against the code book.

name: SpecGen LLM
tagline: Drafts procurement-ready technical specs from a few input parameters.
examplePrompt: Generate a procurement specification for a centrifugal pump rated 500 GPM at 150 ft head, per API 610, including materials and testing requirements.
exampleResult: Full spec draft generated — 6 sections (scope, design, materials, testing, documentation, inspection), ready for review.
how: Template-driven document generator, structured against common procurement-spec formats and equipment codes (API, ASME).
forWhat: First-draft technical specifications for equipment procurement, so engineers start from structure instead of a blank page.
where: Used to draft pump, tank, and piping specs for engineering consulting deliverables.
when: Built Q2 2024, in regular use since Q3 2024.
why: The first draft of a spec is mostly boilerplate structure — this gets that structure right on the first pass.

name: DraftBot 3D
tagline: Turns a plain-language part description into live Fusion360 parameters.
examplePrompt: Generate a parametric flange in Fusion360 — 200mm PCD, 8x M12 bolt holes, ANSI B16.5 Class 150.
exampleResult: Flange model generated — 8x M12 clearance holes on 200mm PCD, 20mm face thickness, confirmed against the B16.5 Class 150 table.
how: Python backend bridging LLM output to the Autodesk Fusion360 API, translating described geometry into real sketch and feature parameters.
forWhat: Direct, deterministic 3D model generation and parametric edits — flanges, brackets, structural members — driven by a text description.
where: Tested generating flange, bracket, and frame-member geometry against Fusion360 desktop.
why: Standard LLMs can describe a part; they can't place a hole on an exact bolt circle. This gives the AI real geometric control instead of a description of one.

name: Simula VR Instructor
tagline: Builds structured VR training scenarios from a procedure description.
examplePrompt: Create a VR training module for confined-space entry on an offshore tank inspection, including hazard checkpoints and pass criteria.
exampleResult: 6-step VR module generated with 3 mandatory hazard checkpoints and a scored completion gate at 80%.
how: Scenario-scripting layer that outputs structured training steps and hazard checkpoints, formatted for VR training engines.
forWhat: Turning a written safety procedure into a checkpointed VR training scenario, for confined-space and working-at-height tasks.
where: Piloted for offshore inspection and confined-space entry training scenarios.
when: Built Q1 2025, in pilot since Q2 2025.
why: Procedures live in PDF form until someone builds the training scenario by hand — this turns the procedure directly into a scorable module.
